messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • High DNS failures + 5xxs observed in eu-west-2 (AZ-B)

incident-bot: Severity: Sev2
incident-bot: Symptom: spike in service 5xx + DNS NXDOMAIN/timeout from host-level checks in AZ-B
incident-bot: Runbook: Network egress -> paging oncall
incident-bot: Link: https://redwood.incidents/2100001234

ari: seeing the pager. i'm on it. paging oncall now -> @sanjay @morgan

oncall-pager: Paging @sanjay (oncall) — please acknowledge

sanjay: acked. grabbing initial metrics. can someone paste the 5xx graph? :eyes:

morgan: pushing graphs -> api-frontend 5xx rate up 4.2% in az-b last 6m, p50 latency normal, p95 slightly up. Cloud DNS errors up ~30% from az-b

ari: logs show lots of `dial udp 53: i/o timeout` from sidecars in az-b. traceroute shows responses returning via az-c sometimes

jamie: we just rolled out a security egress policy at 02:05 (terraform) to tighten outbound DNS to our managed resolvers. possibly related. terraform run id: tf-2026-07-12-azb-egress

sanjay: copying that. can you paste the tf diff?

jamie: diff snippet:
```
resource "aws_network_acl_rule" "deny_udp_outside" {
  cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  protocol   = "17"
  rule_action = "deny"
  rule_number = 100
  egress = true
  from_port = 53
  to_port = 53
}
```

ari: oof — that denies all UDP/53 egress from the subnet's NACLs. our VPC resolver is at .2 and uses UDP/53. That would break DNS.

morgan: confirmed: `dig @172.31.0.2 example.com` from affected host times out. from az-c it succeeds.

sanjay: looks like the NACL was applied only to AZ-B subnets, not the others — explains cross-az fallback and asymmetric routing. immediate mitigation: add allow rule for UDP/53 to VPC DNS and do not rely on SG only.

ari: i'm going to add a temporary NACL allow rule via console now — will also open a quick SSH to bastion to validate with dig after change

ops-bot: running change: aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abcd --rule-number 100 --protocol 17 --port-range From=53,To=53 --egress --rule-action allow

ari: change applied. pls verify

morgan: testing: `dig @172.31.0.2 example.com` -> returns 93.184.216.34 within 70ms

jamie: monitoring graphs — DNS errors drop to baseline within 30s, 5xxs trending down

sanjay: good. mark mitigation: temporary NACL allow for UDP/53 to VPC resolver added. Next: roll back the deny rule and replace with targeted allow-list in tf or use Security Group on the resolver endpoint.

ari: i'm going to create an emergency tf rollback PR to revert the deny and implement a scoped allow for the resolver IPs only. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/terraform/pull/4567

morgan: customer impact update: affected requests mainly from az-b; estimated ~3% of total traffic during window. CS reports 2 customer tickets for elevated latency/timeouts. no large customer downtime reported.

customer-success: noted — i'll reply to the 2 affected customers with ETA ~1h and mitigation steps. thanks.

sanjay: assign ownership: infra-network to own full rollback and permanent fix. oncall will follow up in postmortem. postmortem owner: @jamie

jamie: acknowledged. will include: root cause (overbroad NACL deny in tf), timeline, impact, mitigation, and action items (add NACL test harness + pre-deploy smoke for DNS; require canary for region-limited network changes; review runbooks)

ari: adding a short blameless note: this was a policy change that missed the VPC DNS special-case. we'll update terraform modules to have explicit allow rules for AmazonProvidedDNS and a unit test.

oncall-pager: @sanjay handing off to @morgan for overnight watch. next oncall: morgan (starts in 30m) — please ack

morgan: acked taking over monitoring. will keep an eye for 2h then hand back

ops-bot: Scheduled ticket created: INC-2100001234

incident-bot: Incident status -> Mitigated. Monitoring.

sanjay: closing timeline note here. last checkin: 2100004234

--- end of thread ---
